title: Illness in 1924-25 at the New Orleans Country Club; giving up the horn
summary: Charles describes the spell that struck him leading his orchestra at afternoon tea, and the Maple Leaf band's violin and clarinet players.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: I don't have it no more. I gave it up the very time that I gave up music, I gave it up. You see I got sick in 1924. Well I'll declare. And in 25 the doctor claimed that I would never be able to handle that instrument anymore. Is that right? And I went through it anyhow. I played it up until 25. You see I got sick in 24. But I played it until 25. I got sick in the New Orleans country club. I was playing the afternoon tea, you know, I used to play afternoon tea too. Not only dinner dance but we used to play afternoon tea. That's for those rich people sitting down eating there, you see what I mean? They used to just entertain them. Well I can imagine. And I was there leading my orchestra just that way, just that way. They were all sitting down playing. And I was right in front of them there leading them, you know. And all of a sudden the spell took me. And I just didn't do anything else but just couldn't take myself and sit down like this. And so the violin player, because I always had a violin player in my orchestra, you see. And he asked me, he said, gee Charles, what's the man with you? What's the man with you? I said nothing at all. I said keep the band going. And nobody in the world knew that I was sick but my orchestra right there. That was my own orchestra then, that was Charles' orchestra, you see. Because after the Maple Leaf band broke up, then I had to put up my own band.
They didn't have any violin with the Maple Leaf, huh? The Maple Leaf?
Yeah, did you tell me? We used to use Begar. Sure, we used Begar. Which one? That was Emil Begar.
Yeah, not the drum or the clarinet.
The clarinet was, we used to play with me too, that's Albany. Yeah.
